271112814_a37c8054.text: Our integrated dataset has unveiled 36 different cell types that encompass all major and rare cell types found in the hypothalamic regions, including intermediate progenitor cells that had not been identified in any individual dataset (Figure 3D). Intermediate progenitor cells a population of neural stem cells, are pivotal for their crucial role in neurogenesis as they differentiate into excitatory and/or inhibitory neurons. Our identification of these cell types relied on the co-expression pattern of specific marker genes. Notably, we observed the coexpression of Mki67 (a marker gene for proliferation), Sox2 (a marker gene for neural precursor cells), and Hmgb2, which encodes a chromatin-related transcription activator that is crucial for the transition of neural stem cells from quiescence to proliferative status (Hao et al., 2022; Figure 3B).
